problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 7 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -7 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ 12\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ 12\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=3 \\ 3{x}_{2}=-6 \\ -3{x}_{1}+12{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & -6 \\ -3 & 12 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & k+9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & k+9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k+9.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k+9\,⇒\,k=-9.
$$
